versions.description_html:
Learn what Microsoft's Semantic Kernel is, how plugins and function calling work, and how to connect your code to LLMs. Plain English guide.

Semantic Kernel is the layer under Microsoft's AI tools that almost nobody explains. It's a free, open-source kit that lets your own code talk to a large language model, and lets that model call your code back.

In this episode of Simply Explained you will learn:
  • What Semantic Kernel Actually Is
  • The Kernel and the Name
  • Plugins and Functions
  • Planning and Function Calling
  • Memory and RAG
  • Connectors and Prompts
  • One Kit, Three Languages
  • Copilot, Foundry, and What Comes Next
  • When to Use Semantic Kernel
  • The Recap and One Question

Simply Explained by M365.FM breaks down Microsoft 365, Azure and modern IT topics in clear, jargon-free language. Hosted by Mirko Peters.

Explore more on M365.FM

  • From Financial Data to AI-Ready Decisions: Power BI, Microsoft Fabric, Semantic Models & AI Agents with Rishi Sapra [MVP]
